title: Acquire the complete ITO-etching wastewater recovery study and supplement (C5GC01244A)

response.title: Acquire the complete ITO-etching wastewater recovery study and supplement (C5GC01244A)
response.body:
The deferred source is Swain et al. (2015), *Treatment of indium-tin-oxide etching wastewater and recovery of In, Mo, Sn and Cu by liquid–liquid extraction and wet chemical reduction: a laboratory scale sustainable commercial green process*, [DOI 10.1039/C5GC01244A](https://doi.org/10.1039/C5GC01244A). Its title and publisher abstract identify a potentially distinct manufacturing-wastewater feed and an abiotic recovery process. Complete methods, figures, tables and supplement have not been acquired, so no record or numerical recovery claim was created from this lead.

Actual legitimate routes checked on 2026-10-14:

- The RSC full-text route redirected to the abstract; it did not supply complete methods.
- The publisher-advertised 18-page accepted-manuscript endpoint, `https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/getauthorversionpdf/C5GC01244A`, returned HTTP 403 through the public downloader and web tool. The initial sandbox DNS failure is retained separately from that actual network response.
- The linked supplement, `https://www.rsc.org/suppdata/c5/gc/c5gc01244a/c5gc01244a1.pdf`, returned HTTP 404 in the web tool.
- The OpenAlex DOI lookup succeeded but listed only the closed publisher location, with no repository full-text route. This is a bounded location check, not proof that no lawful copy exists.

Next work should use a newly available legitimate publisher/institutional/author route or an authorized library copy; do not repeat the same blocked endpoints without a changed access condition. Obtain the complete original and original SI, verify file identity/page completeness and retain access dates, licenses where known, hashes, and actual URLs. Then inspect:

1. Whether the experimental solution was actual ITO manufacturing etchant wastewater, a conditioned industrial sample, or a generated/synthetic feed; identify supplier/provenance, mixing, acid composition, pretreatment and initial element inventory.
2. Extraction, scrubbing/stripping and wet-reduction recipes, phase ratios, controls, replication, assay methods and all figure/table/SI mass balances. Distinguish aqueous removal, separated product recovery, purity and total-feed recovery denominators.
3. Impurity disposition, reagent/energy burdens, residual wastewater and scale. Do not inherit the title's commercial/green or abstract zero-pollution claims as demonstrated deployment or comparative performance.
4. Whether a distinct secondary-resource owner is warranted after material/experiment deduplication and an independent saved scientific review. Retain unsupported or conflicting source details explicitly.

The existing elemental **indium** record already uses Nicomel et al. (2020), DOI 10.1039/C9GC03073E, for microalgal adsorption from **synthetic solutions**. That study cannot supply missing real-wastewater evidence for this source. Existing waste LCD panels are a distinct solid feed. The present waste-X-ray-films addition is scientifically separate and does not depend on resolving this issue.

Deduplication used the initial paginated **all-state** issue inventory `/private/tmp/cmm-round80-initial-issues.json` and hidden/ignored/symlink-inclusive searches of records, research, reviews, histories and relevant cited downloads, including normalized DOI and feed names. The coordinator refreshed the paginated all-state inventory immediately before posting; no matching issue was found within those recorded bounds. Evidence/handoff: `research/sources/round80-resources/20261014T194349Z.{md,json}`; raw acquisition/issue-dedup receipts in `/private/tmp/cmm-round80-resources-research/`. This is an open acquisition follow-up, not a defect in the accepted film record.
